title: Condense a procedure used as a tool
statement: When one procedure is used as a tool inside another's step, condense it to one sentence, and run it in full only when it is the procedure being modelled.
example: Called inside a comparison step, a four-step main-idea procedure collapses to one sentence per text.
detail: The procedure spec of a grade 3 reading course names two ways to combine procedures: a sequential chain, where one runs to its final step before the next starts, and a nested call, where a procedure used inside another's step collapses to a single sentence (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/pedagogy/modelling-moment-procedures.md`, line 30). Its example is a cross-text comparison step that calls the main-idea procedure, which then gives one sentence per text rather than its four steps. The rule sits among the spec's design principles.

evidence.quote: The rule: if the whole procedure has its own modelling moment, run it in full. If it is a tool inside another procedure's step, condense to one sentence.
CONNECT Step 2 for cross-text says "use MAIN IDEA" - the MAIN IDEA collapses to one sentence per text, not four steps.
